contents.name: Contents, Section 1.5 Mapping Cones and Cylinders
1.5.1, the mapping cone of a chain map
Exercise 1.5.1, cone(id_C) is split exact with the displayed splitting
Exercise 1.5.2, a map is null homotopic exactly when it extends across cone(C)
contents.reason: This extension criterion is a useful alternate characterization of null homotopy, but the page already imports chain homotopy from HA-2 and does not need a separate extension theorem before the later triangulated discussion.

Corollary 1.5.4, f is a quasi-isomorphism iff cone(f) is exact
Topological Remark, topological cones and mapping cones
contents.reason: The page keeps relative homology purely algebraic and does not import topological cone constructions or cellular-chain identifications from algebraic topology, which the library records elsewhere as deferred subject matter.

contents.name: 1.5.5, the mapping cylinder of a chain map
Exercise 1.5.3, homotopy extension across cyl(C)
Lemma 1.5.6, the target inclusion into cyl(f) is a quasi-isomorphism
Exercise 1.5.4, the retraction cyl(f) -> C and the explicit homotopy to the identity
Topological Remark, topological cylinders and mapping cylinders
contents.reason: The page deliberately stops at chain-level factorization and does not claim the topological mapping-cylinder construction or its cellular identification, which would require a separate algebraic-topology supplier page.

contents.name: the paragraph before Lemma 1.5.7, cyl(f)/B is the mapping cone of f
Lemma 1.5.7, comparison of the cylinder and cone long exact sequences
contents.reason: This result belongs on the next homological-algebra page, where the library builds the connecting morphism and the long exact sequence in homology and checks that the cone-sequence and short-exact-sequence constructions agree.

sources.locator: Section 13.9 "Cones and termwise split sequences" from Definition 13.9.1 through Lemma 13.9.17 (HTML lines 16-205 as opened on Sunday, August 30, 2026).

contents.name: Section 13.9 Cones and termwise split sequences
Definition 13.9.1, the cone of a morphism of complexes
Definition 13.9.1, the canonical morphisms and triangle attached to a cone
Lemma 13.9.2, a homotopy-commuting square induces a morphism of cone triangles in K(A)
the note after Lemma 13.9.2, the induced cone morphism depends on the chosen homotopy
Lemma 13.9.3, factorization through a cone when a composite is homotopic to zero
Definition 13.9.4, termwise split injections and termwise split surjections
Lemma 13.9.5, strictifying a homotopy-commuting square when one leg is termwise split
Lemma 13.9.6, factorization by a termwise split injection with a homotopy-equivalent target
Remark 13.9.7, the explicit homotopy behind Lemma 13.9.6
Lemma 13.9.8, the dual factorization by a termwise split surjection
contents.reason: The HA-3 design uses the source-inclusion mapping-cylinder factorization and does not need the dual split-surjection replacement before the later derived and triangulated pages treat both directions systematically.

contents.name: Definition 13.9.9, the triangle associated to a termwise split exact sequence
contents.reason: This is the entry point for distinguished triangles in the homotopy category, and the HA-3 design explicitly postpones that language until the later triangulated-categories page.

contents.name: Lemma 13.9.10, different splittings give isomorphic associated triangles in K(A)
contents.reason: This independence-of-splitting statement matters when arbitrary distinguished triangles are introduced. The present page uses only the canonical cone triangle and does not yet axiomatize associated triangles from split short exact sequences.

contents.name: Remark 13.9.11, middle maps of split sequences cannot in general be strictified in the category of complexes
Lemma 13.9.12, a certain composite of morphisms between split sequences is zero in K(A)
contents.reason: This technical vanishing statement is tailored to the triangulated-category axioms rather than to the chain-level cone and cylinder interface that HA-3 is building now.

contents.name: Lemma 13.9.13, a morphism of cone triangles is a homotopy equivalence on cones when it is on the outer terms
Lemma 13.9.14, cone triangles and triangles from termwise split sequences agree up to isomorphism and sign
contents.reason: This is exactly the bridge from chain-level cone triangles to distinguished triangles that the HA-3 design says not to impose yet. The later triangulated page is where that sign-sensitive equivalence belongs.

contents.name: Lemma 13.9.15, composable maps can be replaced by termwise split injections up to homotopy equivalence
Lemma 13.9.16, the rotated associated triangle is itself a cone triangle
contents.reason: Rotation of associated triangles is part of the later triangulated-axiom package. The present page records only chain-level cone triangles and their split special cases inside the already-built homotopy category.

contents.name: Lemma 13.9.17, the cone triangle (L, C(f), K[1]) comes from the canonical split short exact cone sequence

contents.name: Contents, Sections 2.7 Complexes and 2.8 Total complexes
Remark 2.7.12, an exact sequence of complexes is exact degreewise
Theorem 2.7.13, the long exact sequence in cohomology of a short exact sequence of complexes
contents.reason: The next homological-algebra page is exactly where the library builds the connecting morphism and long exact sequence machinery. HA-3 uses cone and cylinder constructions without yet turning them into the general long exact sequence package.

contents.name: Definition 2.7.14, chain homotopy and null-homotopy
Proposition 2.7.15, homotopic maps induce the same maps on homology
Definition 2.8.3, the degree of a term in a double complex
Definition 2.8.4, the total sum complex with the alternating-sign differential
Definition 2.8.4, the total product complex
contents.reason: The present page only uses finite direct-sum totalizations implicit in cones and cylinders. Product totalizations belong with the later double-complex and convergence page, where infinite totalization choices become mathematically load-bearing.

contents.name: Remark 2.8.5, the alternating-sign total differential squares to zero
Definition 2.8.6, quadrant and half-plane double complexes
contents.reason: Quadrant and half-plane support conditions are not used anywhere on HA-3. They belong to the later double-complex and spectral-sequence infrastructure, not to the present cone and cylinder page.

contents.name: Remark 2.8.7, the geometric description of the quadrants and half-planes
contents.reason: This notation guide is only relevant once the library is actually working with double complexes and convergence regions. HA-3 never states a quadrant or half-plane hypothesis.

contents.name: Remark 2.8.8, first- and fourth-quadrant total sums equal total products
contents.reason: The equality of the two totalization conventions is important later for bounded double complexes and spectral-sequence constructions. It is not part of the chain-level cone or cylinder interface on this page.
